title: Low-Precision Variant Certification & Introspection Harness for Onboarding
creator: Lena Brooks
description: Build a deterministic certification and introspection harness that standardizes how low-precision model variants (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8) are accepted into the model catalog. The harness will run accuracy, perf, and safety probes, produce an immutable ‘variant certificate’ artifact, and publish a verified performance profile usable by Runtime and Console for routing and rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs a canonical pipeline (microbenchmarks, eval prompts, and safety scans) against a candidate artifact and emits a certificate JSON with metrics and metadata.

Certificate schema documented and accepted by SDK/runtime teams; certificate contains model hash, quant-method, kernel hint, P50/P95/P99 latencies, throughput, tokens/s, token-cost estimate, top-level accuracy metrics (EM/F1/ROUGE/perplexity as applicable), and safety flags.
Automated regression detection: new variant runs are compared to pinned baseline and generate pass/fail given thresholds; failures produce a regression report and block publish.

Integration with CI: a job in serving-runtime CI can produce a candidate certificate and attach it to the PR; untrusted artifacts are not surfaced to production catalogs until human review and a successful canary.
Canary rollout plan documented with clear metric thresholds and automatic rollback hooks in Console and routing layer.
Telemetry hooks implemented so Console dashboards show certificate-linked metrics and compare live canary traffic to baseline.
Documentation and runbook for oncall and SRE describing how to interpret certificate fields and handle failures during canary.
Example certificates for INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8 variants added to dev-docs for reference.
tasks: Design certificate schema and field contracts (owners: Diego, Asha)
Implement harness runner: workload generator, cached-prefix tests, and deterministic microbench suite
Create accuracy/eval adapter that supports both generation metrics and embedding similarity tests
Implement safety checks: prompt-based toxic generation scan and embedding anomaly detector
Add regression comparator that computes delta vectors and decides pass/fail according to policy
Wire CI integration: serving-runtime PR job that emits candidate certificates and uploads to artifacts store
Expose certificate metadata via model-catalog publishing endpoint and Console UI
Draft canary rollout playbook and automatic rollback clauses based on telemetry thresholds
Add docs: developer onboarding page + example notebooks for running harness locally
updates: 2025-11-20: Initial RFC posted to Confluence with schema proposal and example fields. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Variant+Certificate+RFC
2025-11-25: Design review with Runtime and SDK teams — consensus to keep certificate flat (no nested lists) and include kernel hint + memory footprint metric. Action: Diego to update schema.

2025-12-02: Decided to use mixed workload approach: (1) microbench synthetic sequences for perf contraints; (2) representative prompt sampler from anonymized customer corpus for accuracy/regression. Trade-off: sampler increases run time but yields better real-world regressions.

2025-12-10: Prototype harness implemented in /tools/variant_harness. Ran against small LLMs with GPTQ and INT8; produced initial certificates. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1245

2025-12-15: Regression comparator added — uses bootstrap resampling to produce 95% CI for delta of metric. Early feedback from ML Research: prefer paired test when sample prompts overlap. We'll add paired-test option.

2025-12-22: Safety scanner integrated using internal moderation model; flagged a batch of prompts with elevated toxicity for one GPTQ variant. Decision: block publish until variant owner triages; created follow-up ENG ticket ENG-51310.
2026-01-05: Telemetry contract drafted for P50/P95/P99, throughput (tokens/s), token-cost estimate, and embedding drift score. Dashboard stub: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/model-certificates

2026-01-12: QA run across four candidate variants (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8) completed — INT8 variant showed 6% P95 latency regression vs baseline and failed default canary thresholds. Action: Investigate kernel selection and batch size policy

2026-01-18: Runtime PR adding certificate ingest endpoint merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/78. Certificate JSON stored in artifacts bucket with path pattern artifacts/certificates/<model>-<variant>-<timestamp>.json
2026-01-22: Canary playbook draft completed and reviewed by SRE. Next: schedule canary with Dedicated cluster for a low-traffic customer to validate live telemetry mapping.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Synthetic microbenchmarks may not surface semantic regressions. Mitigation: include sampled anonymized prompts and per-domain prompt sets.
Risk: Certification adds CI runtime cost (~2-4 hours per heavy variant). Mitigation: tiered cert levels (quick-smoke vs full-cert) and caching intermediate artifacts.
Risk: False positives from safety scanner block good variants. Mitigation: add human-in-the-loop triage step and clear override policy in catalog UI.

Risk: Live performance differs from harness (hardware/kernel differences). Mitigation: include hardware hints in certificate and require hardware match for automatic routing; otherwise mark as "live-validated": false.
Risk: Large volume of certificates may clutter catalog. Mitigation: add retention policy and pinning; only last N certified variants per model are shown by default.
metrics_to_track: Perf: P50/P95/P99 latency on canonical microbench and representative sampler
Cost: estimated tokens-per-dollar across typical workload mix
Accuracy: delta on canonical eval suite (paired when possible)
Safety: fraction of prompts flagged for toxic or disallowed content
Canary: relative change in user-facing error rate, latency SLO breaches, and embedding drift compared to baseline
references: Related Linear tickets: ENG-4721 (quant profiles onboarding), ENG-31245 (calibration onboarding), ENG-21803 (profile artifact format)
